title: Planning and acting
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Are you planning to avoid acting, or acting without a plan?

Jose described a four-step bootcamp he teaches to young people between ten and eighteen. Step one is mindset: I can, I will. Step two is visualization of your dream and goals, very specifically, with journaling. Step three is process: the business plan, financial plan and job descriptions. Step four is execution, which boils down to making decisions.
He said we have taken action before planning, and planned without taking action. Where do you think the balance is?

A student said: at the start I wanted the presentations and the website perfect, and there were always excuses that I was not ready. Letting that go and just doing it, posting and walking into stores and talking to people, was much better, because what I was thinking was not reality, only what I thought was reality.

Jose said that people who are very organized and granular, and people who act now, create tension, and that there will always be that tension in a company. He said he had planned and not acted on a book he had been writing for years, out of fear of failure.
A student said: not everyone is the best at everything. If there were a bunch of Joses in a company it would be crazy. People who balance each other make a team better than one person.

Jose said that an older mentor told him he was there to make sure that when Jose had an idea he was not drinking the Kool-Aid, intoxicated with an idea only he lived in. That is why you put together a board of advisors and friends whose opinion you respect.
Who is your reality check, and would you listen?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a plan you have not started.
Write the decision that would start it.
Write who is your opposite on this and what they would say.
Write who could be your reality check.
Write the first action for today.

check.q: What is step four of Jose's bootcamp?
What did a student say was not reality?
What did Jose say a board of advisors helps with?

recap: Mindset, picture, process, then decide. Keep a reality check.
